note: Ed25519 verdicts pinned for keypair.verifyIdentityStrict (strict: its byte checks, then @noble/ed25519 2.3.0 verify with zip215:false), for that noble call alone (noble) and for noble's default (loose: zip215:true, what keypair.verifyIdentity uses). Deterministic: fixed seeds sha256("ssf-ed25519-strict-vector-v1|<name>") and fixed scalars. pub and sig are base64url, msg is hex. honest: an ordinary signature. torsion-r: R = 123456789·B + T8 (T8 of order 8), S = r + k·a; the cofactored equation accepts it in both modes. s-plus-l: an honest signature with S + L in place of S. noncanonical-r: R is the order-4 point T4 = 2·T8 (y = 0) spelled with y = p, S = k·a; its canonical spelling passes strict. small-order-key: the key is T8 and (42·B, 42) verifies every message under it. identity-r: R is the identity point (01 00…00) and S = SHA-512("")·a; noble 2.3.0 drops the message from k when R is the identity (R.toBytes() throws inside its try), so under an ordinary key this one signature verifies every message in both noble modes, and verifyIdentityStrict refuses any identity R before calling noble. identity-r-rfc: the same R with S = SHA-512(R‖A‖M)·a, valid under RFC 8032 and in the WebCrypto of Node 22 but refused by noble and by verifyIdentityStrict. strict is the verdict of verifyIdentityStrict, noble is @noble/ed25519 2.3.0 with zip215:false on its own (they differ only for identity-r), loose is the noble default. A change to any verdict means the verifier changed: pages on different versions would fold different rounds.
